items.title: A New Oilsands Pipeline? What Politicians Won’t Admit
items.description: An energy expert lays out the risks and fallacies as Canada and the world fail to face the climate crisis.

items.title: What this surgeon from Ukraine is learning in Canada about treating war victims
items.description: Dr. Mariia Kuzeikiv, an Ukrainian surgeon, is learning skills that could help her save lives in the war while in Hamilton, Ont.

items.title: Homeowner says she’s out $381K after hiring Ottawa contractor to renovate kitchen
items.description: An Ottawa couple says they’ve lost out on more than $381,000 after hiring Ottawa contractor Giuseppe "Joey" Peloso and his company Magnolia to renovate their kitchen, when plumbing broke and flooded their home. Plaintiffs in other lawsuits against Peloso and his business include other customers, subcontractors, investors, the Republic of Austria and Embassy of Niger.

items.title: Olympic runner Moh Ahmed wins his 1st Canadian cross-country title
items.description: In his long-awaited return to the Canadian cross-country championships, Olympic track medallist Moh Ahmed took control late in the open men’s 10-kilometre race and won in 29 minutes 30.4 seconds at Fanshawe Golf Course on Saturday in London, Ont.

items.title: On Our Radar: Buddie turns its completely understandable stress into something beautiful
items.description: Guitar bands are back in Vancouver, and it’s beautiful.

items.title: Why excavators may be a tool of choice for some cash-seeking thieves
items.description: This unique form of theft has been happening all over the Greater Toronto Area and beyond. Thieves on the hunt for cash break through the walls of banks using excavators that experts say anyone capable of ordering a key online can drive off the lot.

items.title: Pay high duties or lose U.S. shoppers? Some Canadian retailers forced to choose amid holiday sales
items.description: Months after the U.S. ended duty-free shipping on small packages, Canadian online retailers will have to make a tough gamble: pay pricey fees on low-value shipments, or get a holiday sales boost from American customers?

items.title: Indigenous groups remain split on Alberta's pipeline pact with feds
items.description: The Alberta Indigenous Opportunities Corporation was named a key partner in Ottawa and Alberta's MOU on on Friday for a pipeline to the B.C. coast, but others have concerns.

items.title: WestJet and Air Transat passengers fight back after airlines falsely claim they can’t film disputes
items.description: Jason Huang says a WestJet employee grabbed his phone and threatened to deny him boarding when he began recording his conversation during airport check-in. Legal expert say passengers are within their rights to record these interactions, and video and audio recordings may help in battles for compensation.

items.title: Between Breaths dives into the life of a Newfoundland conservationist who loved people as much as whales
items.description: "What is your life, and what is your life to you in its final moments?"
